title: Trajectory event family (data payloads of the model.* events + the outcome carrier)
description: The data contracts for the model.* event family in the campaign event log plus the harness-written outcome event (the training-metadata carrier, written by trajectory.record_outcome). The model boundary (model_boundary.py) writes the model.* events directly and its payloads already conform; this schema makes the contracts CHECKABLE after the fact: trajectory.verify_trajectory re-validates every registered event's data against its definition, so a hand-written or drifted event that skips the version stamps (prompt_version, context_hash, payload_sha256, request_sha256) is flagged even though the hash chain itself still verifies. Definitions only — one per event type; the envelope definition documents the hash-chained frame Campaign.log produces and is not enforced per event.

prompt_version.description: sha256[:16] of the system prompt file actually sent (model_boundary.prompt_version)

playbook_id.description: e.g. oracle_manipulation.v1, or null when no playbook matched

visibility_policy.description: the role's field allow-list name, e.g. ["critic-allowlist-v1"]

response_schema.description: the contract the model's output must satisfy (model_response.schema.json definitions)

context_hash.description: sha256 of the canonical serialization of the context bundle actually sent

kind.description: the response kind that failed its contract

error.description: the first failure pointer (record_rejection truncates at 1000 chars)

payload_sha256.description: hash of the rejected payload — the content is the model's, the log records it by hash only

action.description: the re-request instruction, e.g. record_rejection's 're-request against the response contract; do not coerce'

response_schema.description: the contract the accepted payload satisfied

payload_sha256.description: hash of the accepted payload as applied

applied_ref.description: the finding id the response was applied to, or null when nothing was applied

finding_id.description: the finding the response was produced for, when one exists

steps.description: number of plan steps received (mirrors the plan contract's bounds)

tools.description: the distinct tool ids the plan cites; membership in the tool registry was checked at the boundary

snapshot_id.description: the EXACT pinned snapshot; the request must not drift the deployment

execution_profile.description: one of the eight sandbox profiles the harness executes under

request_sha256.description: sha256 of the canonical serialization of the exact validated request handed to the harness

finding_id.description: the finding the reproducer run is for (also carried as the event ref)

outcome.description: The training-metadata carrier (trajectory.record_outcome): the gold outcome a campaign run concluded for one finding, with the training-partition decision derived from the linked eval case. Unlike the model_* definitions it is harness-written, not model traffic, but it is registered in the same event-type map (trajectory.MODEL_EVENT_TYPES), so model_trajectory projects it (role: null) and verify_trajectory validates it with the same machinery.
the gold outcome label the run concluded — the evaluation_case gold.outcome enum plus 'unfinished' for a run that reached no verdict

final_status.description: the finding's status in the findings.py state machine when the outcome was recorded (terminal for a concluded run; the schema cannot check the vocabulary — record_outcome does)

final_evidence_tier.description: the evidence-ladder level the finding had reached when the outcome was recorded

finding_id.description: the finding the outcome closes (also carried as the event ref)

case_id.description: the eval-store case the campaign is linked to, when one exists; null for a standalone campaign. A present-but-unreadable case fails CLOSED (training excluded) — the leakage partition is hard.

training.description: the training-usability decision for this outcome row, derived by record_outcome from the linked case's partition (held-out/training -> hidden + excluded; dev or no case id -> visible; unreadable -> fail closed)

visibility.description: whether the row may surface in default training exports

exclude_reason.description: why the row is kept out of training; required non-null when excluded is true (if/then below)

at.description: UTC ISO-8601 timestamp when the outcome was recorded

event_envelope.description: DOCUMENTATION ONLY — the hash-chained envelope Campaign.log produces around every event (state.py _event_hash). The data payload inside is validated against one of the model_* definitions above, or against the outcome definition for the harness-written outcome event.

ref.description: optional primary reference id (e.g. the finding id)

data.description: the event payload — one of the model_* definitions above for model.* events

event_hash.description: canonical sha256 over every other field
